summary: java.util.NoSuchElementException ticking entity crash when a workstation is destroyed near a villager with a job
description: NOTE: This bug is different from MC-145686, but could be related. MC-145686 was about java.util.Optional.get(Optional.java:135), this one is about it.unimi.dsi.fastutil.longs.LongLinkedOpenHashSet.removeFirstLong (LongLinkedOpenHashSet.java:470) gotten in a near-similar environment. Environment Have a villager with a job near a workstation (preferably within a 1-block radius). Attached ( ) is the world I used. At -83 / -12 is a pit with a villager. This is where I performed my testing. How to reproduce To trigger the crash, one commonly needs to quickly destroy and place the workstation. This will cause the villager to quickly switch from being a nitwit and the job belonging to the workstation. In the snapshots of 1.14, this crash seems to be fairly easy to reproduce, as the villager keeps its job for longer or even doesn t become a nitwit once its workstation is destroyed. In 1.14.2, villagers switch quickly between nitwit and having a job, thus it requires more destroying and placing (and more time to reproduce). Suggestion is, taken from the comments about this bug on MC-145686, to map the place and destroy buttons to keys near each other, for example E and F for placing and destroying, respectively. Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition.  
2. Create a new Singleplayer world in Creative mode with default settings.  
3. Open chat and execute `/time set 2000` to set the time of day.  
4. Execute `/summon minecraft:villager ~ ~ ~` to spawn a villager near you.  
5. In Creative inventory, select a lectern (a workstation without a GUI) and place it within one block of the spawned villager.  
6. Stand very close to the lectern, aim at the side of the block nearest you, then press and hold the right‑mouse button followed by the left‑mouse button repeatedly to break and immediately replace the lectern as quickly as possible.  
7. Observe that the game crashes and a crash report is generated containing `java.util.NoSuchElementException` with a stack trace referencing `LongLinkedOpenHashSet.removeFirstLong`.
Observed Behavior: When a villager that already has a profession is positioned within one block of its workstation and the player repeatedly breaks and replaces that workstation the server crashes with a java.util.NoSuchElementException originating from it.unimi.dsi.fastutil.longs.LongLinkedOpenHashSet.removeFirstLong while the world is being ticked; the stack trace shows the exception propagating through ckn.b, aqh$a.a, aqh.a, us.a, ve.a, vg.a and finally MinecraftServer.b, causing the server to halt. In snapshots of 1.14 the crash is easy to reproduce because the villager retains its job for a longer period after the block is destroyed, whereas in 1.14.2 the villager flips quickly between being a nitwit and having a profession, which requires more rapid destroy‑place cycles to trigger the failure. The issue has been observed since snapshot 19w14b and does not appear in 19w14a. The crash can be reproduced in creative mode by spawning a villager, setting the time to night, placing a non‑GUI workstation such as a lectern nearby, and then holding the right‑click and left‑click mouse buttons to break and replace the block repeatedly; after a few iterations the server throws the NoSuchElementException and stops. The problem is distinct from MC‑145686, which involved an Optional.get error, but the two may be related because both occur in a similar environment where a villager’s workstation status changes rapidly.
Expected Behavior: When the workstation block is rapidly broken and replaced while a villager with the corresponding profession stands within one block, the game should handle the job change gracefully: the villager loses its profession (becoming a nitwit) when the block is removed, regains the profession when the block is placed again, and the server continues ticking without throwing a NoSuchElementException or crashing.
